prompt: Which dock “lists the active scene's nodes”?
explain: The Scene dock shows the nodes of the scene you have open, as a tree.

prompt: Which dock “allows you to edit the properties of a selected node”?
explain: The Inspector shows the properties of the node you have selected, and you change them there.

prompt: Which dock “lists your project files, including scripts, images, audio samples, and more”?
explain: The FileSystem dock lists the files of your project: scripts, images, sounds and the rest.

prompt: What sits in the center of the editor, “below the scene selector”, with its toolbar at the top?
explain: The viewport is the center of the editor, under the scene tabs, with its toolbar at the top and docks on either side.

prompt: Which main screen do you use “for all types of games”, and is “where you'll build your interfaces”?
explain: The 2D screen is for every kind of game: besides 2D games, it is where interfaces are built.

prompt: Which main screen “is a complete code editor with a debugger, rich auto-completion, and built-in code reference”?
explain: The Script screen is the editor's own code editor, with a debugger and built-in code reference.

prompt: At the top of the viewport, where do you “find different tools to move, scale, or lock the scene's nodes”?
explain: The toolbar sits at the top of the viewport and changes with the context and the selected node.

prompt: What, “situated below the viewport, is the host for the debug console, the animation editor, the audio mixer, and more”?
explain: The bottom panel holds tools such as the debug console, folded until you click one.

prompt: Which main screen “is where your project will appear when running it from the editor”?
explain: The Game screen shows your running project; changes made there are not saved when it stops.

prompt: Along the editor's top edge, what sits on the right, beside the Movie Maker Mode toggle?
explain: The playtest buttons sit at the right of the editor's top edge, beside the Movie Maker Mode toggle.

prompt: “Just below the workspace buttons”, what shows each opened scene, with a plus (+) button beside them to add a new one?
explain: The opened scenes show as tabs under the workspace buttons; the plus (+) button adds a new scene.

prompt: “By default, along the window's top edge”, what sits on the left?
explain: The main menu sits at the left of the editor's top edge, with the workspace buttons in the center.

prompt: In which main screen can you “work with meshes, lights, and design levels for 3D games”?
explain: The 3D screen is where 3D levels are built from meshes and lights.

prompt: “When you launch Godot”, what is “the first window you see”?
explain: The Project Manager opens first; there you manage, import or create projects before the editor opens.

prompt: Which main screen “is a library of free and open source add-ons, scripts, and assets to use in your projects”?
explain: The Asset Library is the fifth main screen, where community add-ons and assets are found.

prompt: Godot comes with it built in: press F1 anywhere in the editor to search it for “a class, method, property, constant, or signal”. What is it?
explain: The built-in class reference opens an item's page in the Script screen when you double-click it in the search.
